The figure above shows the graph of a piecewise linear function $y=f(x).$ The point $A$ has coordinates $(2,0)$ and lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $(0,2)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x),$ what is $({f}^{-1})^{′}(0)?$

$({f}^{-1})^{′}(0)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Since $(0,2)$ lies on ${f}^{-1},$ we have ${f}^{-1}(0)=2.$ 
The slope of the tangent to $f(x)$ for $x\in [0,4]$ is $\frac{1}{2}$, hence, ${f}^{′}(2)=\frac{1}{2}.$

The formula for the derivative of the inverse function is 

$$
({f}^{-1})^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(x))}.
$$

Evaluating at $x=0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(0) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(0))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(2)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
